title: Arrow dg category comparison for trivial cofibrations
statement:
Use dg categories, quasi-equivalences and $\mathsf{Hqe}$ (the ordinary localization at quasi-equivalences) as in [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure], and the complex-enriched model conventions of [lem-coef-enriched-projective-diagram-model], in universes large enough for all categories below. Let $\mathcal M$ be a category enriched over cochain complexes of abelian groups with a model structure satisfying the enriched model axiom stated there; suppose all its objects are fibrant. Let $\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal M$ be a full subcategory closed under weak equivalences in both directions, and let $\operatorname{Int}(\mathcal S)$ be its full dg subcategory on cofibrant objects. Define $\mathcal E_{\mathcal S}$ to have objects the trivial cofibrations $c:P\to Q$ with $P,Q$ cofibrant in $\mathcal S$, and morphism complexes
$$\mathcal E_{\mathcal S}(c,c')=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P,P')\times_{\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P,Q')}\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(Q,Q'),$$
where $c':P'\to Q'$ and the maps to the middle complex are postcomposition by $c'$ and precomposition by $c$. Differential and composition are componentwise. This defines a dg category. The source projection $e_0:\mathcal E_{\mathcal S}\to\operatorname{Int}(\mathcal S)$ is surjective on objects and degreewise a surjective quasi-isomorphism on every morphism complex. The target projection $e_1$ is also a quasi-equivalence. The identity-arrow dg functor $s:\operatorname{Int}(\mathcal S)\to\mathcal E_{\mathcal S}$ satisfies $e_0s=e_1s=1$, and $[e_0]=[e_1]$ in $\mathsf{Hqe}$. Thus for any small dg category $\mathcal A$ and any strict dg functor $T:\mathcal A\to\mathcal E_{\mathcal S}$, the composites $e_0T,e_1T$ define the same morphism in $\mathsf{Hqe}$.
